stories.title: AI imaging tracks glioblastoma cell movement
stories.summary: Researchers at Uppsala University have combined live imaging and artificial intelligence to track how individual glioblastoma cells spread through brain tissue. The method reveals how cells switch movement patterns and respond to treatments. The brain has been asked to show its work.

stories.title: Genetic cause of fatal newborn brain disorder identified
stories.summary: Researchers at King Abdullah University of Science and Technology and King Faisal Specialist Hospital and Research Center have identified a previously unknown cause of a fatal newborn brain disorder. The discovery provides long-awaited answers to affected families. The mystery has been solved.

stories.title: Study finds thousands of new genetic variants affecting drug response
stories.summary: A study of nearly 100,000 Americans identified thousands of new variants in genes that influence drug responses. Using data from the NIH All of Us program, researchers found every participant carried at least one variant. Genetic data is being used to personalize treatments.

stories.title: Protein identified as potential target for Chagas disease
stories.summary: Researchers at the University of São Paulo have identified a protein target to interrupt the infection cycle of the Trypanosoma cruzi parasite. Laboratory tests suggest the protein could be used to develop new Chagas disease treatments. The parasite has been interrupted.

stories.title: Researchers map heart lymphatic vessel development
stories.summary: Researchers at Children's Hospital Los Angeles have identified molecular signals that shape the heart's network of lymphatic vessels. The study offers insight into how these vessels form and respond to injury. The heart's plumbing is becoming clearer.

stories.title: Gut antibodies may protect against colon cancer
stories.summary: Rockefeller University scientists have discovered that antibodies coating the gut lining may play a role in preventing colon cancer. The findings suggest a protective function for the immune system in the digestive tract. The gut is defending itself.

stories.title: LJI launches functional genomics database
stories.summary: The La Jolla Institute for Immunology has launched the Functional Immunogenomics and Transcriptomics database. Directed by Assistant Professor Miguel Reina-Campos, the resource is designed to serve as a hub for immune cell research. The immune system is being cataloged.

stories.title: Review examines oral PCSK9 drug for high cholesterol
stories.summary: A review from Binghamton University explores the use of Lipfendra, an oral PCSK9 inhibitor, for patients who cannot tolerate injectable medications. The findings were published in the Annals of Pharmacotherapy. Needle-free options are being reviewed.

stories.title: Melanoma mutations may vary by patient age
stories.summary: A new Yale study suggests that a patient's age may be a factor in which mutations drive melanoma. Precision medicine aims to match treatments to specific tumor genetics. Age is being added to the list of variables.

stories.title: Long COVID recovery rates vary by symptom type
stories.summary: An NIH-funded study found that about half of adults with long COVID saw symptom improvement within three years. Recovery rates were 60 percent for those with smell and taste loss, but under 20 percent for multisystem symptoms. Improvement is not universal.

stories.title: Immune cell subset linked to lung cancer response
stories.summary: Researchers found that gamma-delta T cells can infiltrate small cell lung cancer tumors and kill them without standard MHC-I machinery. Patients with higher levels of these cells trended toward longer survival with immunotherapy. The immune system has a workaround.

stories.title: CRISPR gene editing trial lowers triglycerides
stories.summary: A phase 1b trial found that one-time CRISPR-Cas9 editing of the ANGPTL3 gene lowered triglyceride levels by a mean of 63 percent at 30 days. The results were presented at the American Heart Association Scientific Sessions. The gene was edited.

stories.title: President Murmu presents Swachh Survekshan awards
stories.summary: President Droupadi Murmu presented the Swachh Survekshan Awards 2025-26 in New Delhi. She stated that cleanliness reflects public health, social consciousness, and administrative accountability, and should be a reflection of everyday habits. Cleanliness is being encouraged.

stories.title: New AIIMS facilities record 6 crore consultations
stories.summary: The 18 new All India Institutes of Medical Sciences have recorded approximately 6.01 crore outpatient consultations since 2021-22. The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare says the figures highlight the expanding reach of specialized tertiary healthcare. Access is being expanded.

stories.title: Proposed framework for allied health professionals
stories.summary: The National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Professions has proposed a regulatory framework for the registration of allied health workers. The plan includes pathways for skill upgradation and competency assessment. The sector is being structured.

stories.title: AIIMS digital counter sparks online debate
stories.summary: An AIIMS digital counter displaying population figures has sparked online debate regarding India's population nearing 1.5 billion. Access to the original report is restricted. The counter is being discussed. Further details were thin in the open report.

stories.title: Centre proposes provisional registration for allied health
stories.summary: The National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Professions has proposed a provisional registration framework for allied health workers. The Ministry of Health says the move aims to bring uniformity and accountability to professional registration. The registry is being updated.

stories.title: AIIMS director discusses diabetes misconceptions
stories.summary: AIIMS Director Dr. Nikhil Tandon addressed common questions regarding diabetes, including the risks of belly fat and the nature of pre-diabetes. He noted that remission is not a cure and clarified the rule of halves. The disease is being explained.

stories.title: Health Ministry proposes new registration framework for allied professionals
stories.summary: The National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Professions has proposed a regulatory framework for the provisional registration of allied health workers. The ministry says the plan aims to ensure transparency and accountability in business registration. It also provides systematic opportunities for working professionals to enhance their skills.

stories.title: India rethinks multidimensional strategies for anaemia prevention
stories.summary: India has seen decades of high anaemia prevalence despite iron and folic acid supplementation. While fortification is a broad strategy, it has not worked in real-world settings and may have adverse effects for unintended populations. The country is now pivoting towards better multidimensional strategies for prevention.

stories.summary: Congress leader Pawan Khera questioned the Centre after air pollution was dropped from a revised agenda for a Parliamentary Standing Committee meeting. The topic had been included in the initial circular on November 5 but was removed from the subsequent version. Public health remains a point of contention.

stories.title: AIIMS population counter sparks viral interest
stories.summary: A digital board at AIIMS Delhi showing a population estimate of 1.48 billion has gone viral. The counter updates every second based on presumptive birth and mortality rates rather than an actual census. It serves as a reminder that the board does not count people.

stories.title: CPCB considers raising monitoring cap after data gaps
stories.summary: The Central Pollution Control Board is considering steps to capture peak particulate matter levels after data from several monitoring stations went missing. Current sensors only measure up to 1,000 units. The gaps led to an artificially lower official air quality index during the recent pollution spike.

stories.summary: The Gaza Health Ministry announced at least eight Palestinians were killed and 29 injured in the past 24 hours. Since the war began in October 2023, the ministry reports 74,653 Palestinians have been killed and 176,007 injured. The full piece is for subscribers.

stories.title: BIMSTEC adopts revised public health plan
stories.summary: BIMSTEC health ministers have adopted a revised plan of action for 2026 to 2030 to improve regional health security. The roadmap outlines cooperation in pandemic preparedness, digital health, and traditional medicine. Union Health Minister Jagat Prakash Nadda represented India at the meeting in Colombo.

stories.title: Congo Ebola outbreak reaches 11,000 cases
stories.summary: The Congo Ebola outbreak has surpassed 11,000 cases with 5,387 deaths, making it the country's deadliest on record. The Bundibugyo strain currently has no approved vaccine or treatment. Fighting in the affected provinces continues to slow the medical response.

stories.title: MSF calls for wider access to Ebola vaccines
stories.summary: Doctors Without Borders is urging global officials to lift restrictions on the Ervebo vaccine in DR Congo. While the vaccine was developed for a different strain, the charity suggests it may provide protection. The country requested 500,000 doses, but only 70,000 were released.

stories.title: JP Nadda represents India as BIMSTEC adopts revised public health plan
stories.summary: The first BIMSTEC Health Ministers’ Meeting took place in Colombo, Sri Lanka, culminating in the unanimous adoption of a Joint Ministerial Statement and the Revised BIMSTEC Plan of Action on Public Health (2026 to 2030). stories.summary: More than 74,600 Palestinians have been killed in Israel’s war on the Gaza Strip since October 2023, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health, as Israeli attacks continue despite a ceasefire. The ministry’s latest figures put the cumulative death toll above 74,600, with more than

stories.summary: Congo's Ebola cases have crossed 11,000 cases in another development that shows the severity of the outbreak. stories.title: Three polio workers abducted in Pakistan
stories.summary: Three polio vaccination workers were abducted by unidentified armed men in northwestern Pakistan on Tuesday. The incident occurred in the Tank district during an ongoing immunisation campaign. This follows a series of similar attacks and abductions targeting vaccination teams in the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa region.

stories.title: Experimental vaccines to join Ebola trial in Congo
stories.summary: World Health Organization experts have recommended two experimental vaccines for inclusion in the ongoing Tumaini trial in DR Congo. The University of Oxford’s ChAdOx1 BDBV and Moderna’s mRNA-1469 will join an existing vaccine to combat the Bundibugyo virus. The outbreak continues to spread.

stories.summary: The National Health Authority has selected EkaCare to deploy an ambient AI voice scribe for doctors in public healthcare facilities. The solution aims to convert consultations into structured digital health records, reducing documentation workloads. The system will operate on NHA infrastructure powered by Amazon Web Services.

stories.title: Government plans AI-led upgrade for Ayushman Bharat
stories.summary: The central government plans to integrate AI to automate insurance claims, improve fraud detection, and digitise medical records. Proposed interventions include greater use of automated claims processing and AI-enabled clinical documentation to strengthen the Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana and the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission.

stories.summary: The National Health Authority (NHA) has selected Bengaluru-based health AI startup EkaCare as a technology partner for its ambient AI-enabled Voice Scribe solution, which aims to reduce documentation for doctors in public health facilities. “With the Voice Scribe, a doctor can speak with the patient

stories.summary: Finite State has raised $27 million in a Series C funding round to scale its autonomous platform. The company aims to help device makers manage software supply chain risks and address a surge of AI-discovered flaws. The round was led by private funds managed by The O.H.I.O. Fund.

stories.title: Parenting app linked to reduction in sexual violence
stories.summary: A digital parenting program reduced sexual violence and exploitation among adolescent girls in Tanzania by more than half, according to research from the University of Oxford. The study suggests the program could also deliver substantial benefits for families. The full piece is for subscribers.

stories.title: Digital mental health adoption linked to education
stories.summary: A study of Palestinian citizens of Israel found that 16.7 percent of surveyed adults used digital mental health services. Adoption was significantly associated with higher education and positive attitudes toward technology. These factors remained relevant even when accounting for clinical symptoms and barriers to in-person care.

stories.title: Youth and caregiver mental health reports differ
stories.summary: A study indicates that reports of mental health issues from youth and their caregivers often differ. Researchers suggest that both perspectives are necessary to form a complete picture of a child's well-being. The full piece is for subscribers.

stories.title: Study links family activities and exercise to resilience
stories.summary: New research suggests that family activities, volunteering and regular exercise are linked to greater psychological resilience. The study highlights these behaviors as potential contributors to mental health. The full piece is for subscribers.

stories.title: Study compares creativity and mental health in twins
stories.summary: A study of 15,000 Swedish twins found that artistic achievement is associated with more mental health difficulties, while scientific creativity is not. If creativity itself caused mental illness, both groups should suffer equally. Apparently, the baggage depends on the tools used to create.

stories.title: Women veterans report higher mental health needs
stories.summary: Nearly half of post-9/11 veterans screened positive for depression, anxiety or PTSD. Women reported more mental health and substance use problems than men, yet did not see a corresponding increase in appointments. The care system has not yet caught up to the reported needs.

stories.title: Weekly park visits linked to better mental health
stories.summary: Children who visit parks at least once a week from birth to age 11 score 16.5 percent better on mental health assessments, according to a University of Exeter study. The research suggests that regular time in playgrounds supports social development. Nature is apparently a scheduled activity.

stories.title: New obesity diagnostic approach proposed
stories.summary: Doctors suggest that combining BMI with organ function tests and other measurements could prevent misdiagnosis in millions. BMI alone reportedly misses obesity in 5 to 9 percent of adults while wrongly diagnosing 3 percent. A blunt instrument is being asked to do more precise work.

research.title: Cancer-fighting chewing gum slashes HPV levels by up to 93%
research.summary: A surprising new weapon against microbes linked to head and neck cancer could be as simple as chewing gum. Scientists developed a bioengineered gum that reduced HPV levels by up to 93% in oral samples from cancer patients and nearly eliminated two harmful bacterial species after a single.

research.title: Energy drinks linked to 11 times more reports of cardiac arrest
research.summary: A new study found that energy drinks and stimulant supplements were linked to disproportionately frequent reports of serious heart problems, including 11 times more reports of cardiac arrest and 4.5 times more reports of heart attacks. Young adults accounted for nearly half of the cardiovascular reports involving these.

research.title: Even occasional marijuana use linked to 40% higher odds of stroke
research.summary: New research involving more than 440,000 Americans links cannabis use to increased cardiovascular risk, with occasional users showing 40% higher odds of reporting a history of stroke. The findings suggest that even infrequent marijuana use may warrant concern, although researchers have not established that cannabis directly causes strokes.

research.title: Lessons from recent investigator-initiated trials of gene-editing therapies in China
research.summary: Nature Medicine, Published online: 11 November 2026, doi:10.1038/s41591-026-04768-x Several deaths during trials of experimental cell and gene therapies in China appear to reveal gaps in governance and oversight. A new layer of independent external review is needed for clinical supervision of high-risk therapies.

research.title: Normalized membrane ratio of TROP2 as a predictor of clinical outcomes with datopotamab deruxtecan in non-small-cell lung cancer
research.summary: Nature Medicine, Published online: 11 November 2026, doi:10.1038/s41591-026-04716-9 This work developed and validated a computational pathology biomarker, the TROP2 normalized membrane ratio, that quantifies subcellular TROP2 localization and predicts improved progression-free and overall survival with datopotamab deruxtecan in patients with nonsquamous non-small-cell lung cancer lacking actionable genomic alterations.

research.title: Obesity linked to up to 27% lower risk of death in dementia
research.summary: A surprising study of more than 4,500 older adults found that people who were overweight or obese when diagnosed with dementia had a 16% to 27% lower risk of death than those at a normal weight. Researchers suspect that extra energy and muscle reserves may help patients survive.

research.title: Scientists find deadly virus DNA hidden in 1,000-year-old manuscripts
research.summary: Ancient manuscripts, including the 1,000-year-old York Gospels, have revealed traces of a deadly sheep virus whose history stretches back more than 3,700 years. Scientists discovered that the virus has remained remarkably unchanged for millennia, turning historic parchment into an unexpected record of ancient disease outbreaks.

research.title: MIT scientists turn immune cells into cancer killers inside the body
research.summary: MIT scientists have developed nanoparticles that reprogram immune cells directly inside the body to attack cancer and harmful immune cells, eliminating tumors and reversing liver damage in mouse experiments. The breakthrough could make powerful immune therapies dramatically simpler and less expensive while opening new possibilities for treating cancer.
